context: seed: every listing route of this API pages (suite/families/curriculum.py:128) — the body is {items, next} and next names the following page or null; every clothing of the paged-api lesson asks for a sum or a count over the whole collection under a budget of the page count plus at most one
counterfactual: The overshoot is summing the first page alone — the naive policy at suite/families/conventions.py:52, suite/families/transfer.py:43 and suite/families/curriculum.py:134 — when the page carries `next` at suite/families/curriculum.py:128; the other overshoot is walking pages the response never named.
decision: A listing route answers a page: an object with `items` and `next`. Aggregate over every page: GET the route, fold its items into the running sum or count, then GET the path that `next` names — verbatim, as given — and repeat until `next` is null. The answer is over all pages; a result from the first page alone is wrong. Spend exactly one call per page: no repeated calls, no probing of `?page=` paths the response did not name, and no /v2 or ?token= on a collection route.

residue: whether an item counts (its active field, its value) is read off the prompt; the rule settles the walk, not the predicate

not_this: a GET of a single resource by id, which answers one object with no items or next
a route under /secure, which needs the token before any page is read
a response whose body is a bare list or an object with no next field — there is nothing further to walk
